notes:
User is building highly detailed, realistic 1/25-scale vehicle models, primarily a Ford Mustang Shelby GT350R and now a Ford F-150 pickup. They use Vallejo paints and are impressed by their color range and quality. They seek practical, authentic advice emphasizing real-car references, correct scale/materials, subtle effects, clean assembly, test fits, and careful layering. Prioritize accuracy and verify product codes, GT350R/F-150 mechanical details, and material instructions rather than making unsupported claims.

Project interests:
- Realistic, restrained weathering: grime in recesses, fading, paint chips, scratches, tire wear, road debris, mud, dust, oil stains, and rust.
- Metallic wheel finishes using thin paint layers, washes, subtle drybrushing/edge highlights, and clear varnish.
- Realistic seatbelts using photo-etched metal strips, fabric/ribbon, tiny buckles/fittings, stitching where appropriate, careful shaping, adhesive assembly, and light weathering.
- Authentic dashboards using reference-based decals, photo-etch, small plastic/metal or 3D-printed parts; gauges, switches/knobs, vents, trim, correct colors/textures, subtle wear, and careful alignment.
- Accurate GT350R engine/transmission detailing: block, heads, intake, exhaust, accessories, transmission case, drivetrain, wiring, hoses, and fuel/coolant lines, followed by tasteful paint/weathering.

Airbrushing guidance discussed for smooth 1/25 car-body coats: clean and prime, use suitable thinned acrylic paint, correct manufacturer pressure/nozzle settings, hold roughly 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) away, maintain a perpendicular angle, use light sweeping strokes and thin coats, allow drying between coats, work in controlled sections, and practice on scrap parts. Smaller nozzles can improve control. Avoid assuming one universal pressure or insisting wet-on-wet is always appropriate.

Decal guidance: confirm scale and decal type, clean surfaces, cut with a sharp blade leaving a border, soak as the decal manufacturer recommends, position carefully, use setting solution and an applicator, work from the center outward on curves, and test first. Apply decals before final clear coat unless the product instructions specify otherwise; use references for exact placement.
